ground water system in the Project Area includes an inventory of springs and existing wells and the drilling of new wells for monitoring purposes. Data were collected on source, yield, use, chemical quality, well depths, and depth to water in the wells (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1).
A number of test wells were installed in the overburden, the coals, the interburden, and the 50 to 150 foot thick section below the Robinson coal. These test wells include five groups of wells in Tract II and nine groups of wells in Tract III. In addition, six wells were drilled in the colluvium and alluvium of Sarpy and East Fork Sarpy Creek valleys.
A group of wells consisted of two or three wells drilled at a location. The wells were cased and sealed so that specific stratigraphic horizons could be sampled for changes in water quality and potentiometric head, thus providing a basis for determining local effects of mining on ground water. The locations of these wells are shown in Appendix D. Since July 1975, water levels have been measured monthly and samples collected for chemical analysis from wells on a periodic basis, ranging from generally every two months to biannually. In order to determine hydrologic characteristics of the units sampled, pumping and packer tests were made to determine transmissivity and lateral permeability. Vertical permeability was determined by laboratory methods for a number of core samples. Geophysical logs were made of the wells and include gamma ray, spontaneous potential, resistivity, velocity (continuous or three dimensional), neutron, density, caliper and temperature logs (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1).
